doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Pharoah's melody, soprano sax and creative recording sessions
summary: Pharoah played soprano for the first time on the piece; sessions with Pharoah and Leon Thomas were free and quick.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: That’s great. What a story. And did Pharoah sort of improvise the melody?

In a way, yeah. Right, right. Because I put a melody to it and copyrighted it, but what happened was, and then someone bought — I was telling the rest of the story and they said, I think that was the first time Pharoah played soprano.
And you did your own version of it on your —
Yeah. And I’m assuming that you sort of wrote out the melody with a little more precision?

Right. And so you know that was it. And we did it. But back then, you know, everything was just more creative. Because we did that whole record in one night and I mean we was just very creative, every time Pharoah and Leon. Leon Thomas always got together. You could start with something and then you just keep exploring and just keep going.
